set.body: The plugin's hook manifest declares its events at the top level, but the loader reads them from under a top-level hooks record. The file is valid JSON, so nothing complained; the loader simply found no events and every hook silently did nothing for anyone who installed the plugin. Four of four other installed plugins use the wrapper. Incorporated from pull request 329, which found it against a real installation.

set.body: A weekly report counts an item as shipped only when a close event falls inside the window. Compaction folds an item's events into a single snapshot, so the close event no longer exists and the item silently drops out of the report even though it closed inside the window. Nightly compaction runs on the default branch, so any work closed more than a day earlier disappears — from precisely the artifact that is supposed to span a week. The close time is not lost: the snapshot's watermark is the last event it folded, which for a closed item is the close itself.
set.title: Compaction hides shipped work from the status report

set.resolution: The window now falls back to the snapshot watermark when a close event has been compacted away. This window read 9 items before the fix and 61 after.

set.body: The verifier asks only whether the cited symbol appears somewhere inside the cited line range. A range that starts at the right line and ends in the wrong place therefore passes, so a reader is pointed at a window that is not the definition. The v0.22.1 documentation regeneration found six citations wrong this way, every one reported as fine.
set.title: doc-verify accepts a citation whose range is merely close

set.resolution: The verifier now checks that a cited range begins where the symbol is defined, not merely that the symbol appears somewhere inside it. The end is deliberately not judged.

set.body: worklog's item is a single positional, so close with two ids quoted together puts both in one string. The resolver already refuses that, but ingest and conflict append without resolving, so the event was written against a key matching no item: exit zero, no output, nothing changed. The sidecar path rendered from that key grows with every id, and one downstream log carried a ten-id key whose filename exceeded the filesystem limit and crashed the doc renderer.
set.title: Composite item ids write junk events on the non-resolving sync commands

set.body: The pre-commit hook reports every citation problem in the repository, and all forty-eight live in frozen documents that policy says stay frozen. The warning therefore fires on every commit forever, regardless of what the commit touched, which teaches people to scroll past it. The hook's own comment already says it reports on documents the commit may not touch.
set.title: The citation warning fires on every commit and can never clear

set.resolution: The hook now checks only documents the commit touches; the repo-wide run stays for the release gate.
Shipped in #341: _require_item now rejects an id containing whitespace, which closes the hole on ingest and conflict — the two commands that append without resolving.

set.body: Release four correctness fixes: the citation verifier now judges where a citation starts, the status report survives compaction, the commit-time citation warning is scoped to what the commit touches, and composite item ids are rejected before they write junk events.
